object_description: an unequal pair of buildings, a single-storey row nestled into the slope and a three-storey block on the street
geometry_property: single-storey row of three identical units
design_condition: the two buildings occupy the edges of the site, the kindergarten row nestling into the slope along the path and the childcare block lining the street, closing the square and freeing open space inside

positive: The programme is read as an unequal pair and consistently assigned to two buildings
A specific building type is selected and developed for each topographical condition
Occupying the edges closes off the square and creates open space inside
Massing and volume formation respond to the immediate neighbourhoods in a big way
The ensemble divides the open space into three different areas
The kindergarten accommodates the height jump to the sports area in a relaxed manner
The distance between kindergarten and path is balanced
The building accommodates the terrain jump using simple structural means
Exterior and interior spaces are thought of in one another and communicated to each other
The route from the path through the front garden and cloakroom structures the sequence and gives an address
It ensures a direct connection to the open space on the ravine side
Interior and exterior spaces are woven together in a direct and easily accessible way
The base hall forms the actual address on the street
The inner staircase connects the hall with the upper outdoor rooms
Both buildings achieve polyvalence comparatively well due to their structural clarity
The kindergartens have an internal connection along the longitudinal axis
The kindergarten trinity, structured and offset in height, is naturally staggered into the area
It comes to a typologically and design-convincing conclusion on the valley side with an outdoor offer
The falling eaves unify and calm the volume on the path side
On the wooded side the volume breaks up in the rhythm of the units and seeks spatial connection outside
This spatial impact is successful, separating as well as connecting and convincingly functional
The materialisation is comprehensible and carefully worked out
The authors succeed in creating an ensemble and a convincing completion of the square
negative: The hedge structure separates the kindergarten groups, reducing coexistence and appearing fragmented
The large overall footprint of the two buildings makes the open space correspondingly smaller
Seen from above the kindergarten building alone threatens to sink
The childcare building loses its massive base, which is missing at this terrain jump
In the more compact building the functionality is more modest and the interweaving is not essential
The comparatively big settlement is the price paid
The design quality of the childcare building does not match that of the kindergarten
Its design elements sometimes appear applied and are suspected of being arbitrary
The roof shape seems due less to local necessity than to the search for analogy
